title: Exact evaluation squares commute with ordinary derived descent
statement: Let A,B,C,T be abelian categories with their ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let U,U':A→B, V:B→T, F:A→C and R,S:C→T be additive exact functors. Fix natural isomorphisms a:UV≅FR and b:U'V≅FS, and chain natural transformations tau:U_c→U'_c and sigma:R_c→S_c. Let I:U_D→U'_D and J:R_D→S_D satisfy the canonical representative factorization equations [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. If V_c(tau_M) followed by b_c equals a_c followed by sigma_(F_c M) for every complex M, then for every X in D(A), a_D inverse followed by V_D(I_X) followed by b_D equals J_(F_D X), where a_D and b_D are the canonical derived isomorphisms formed from composition and derived natural-isomorphism comparisons.

source.place: Tag 015F, exact-functor derived factorization, together with categories.tex Tag 04VG, natural transformations through localization. Agent-formulated compatibility lemma for the finite-evaluation step of lem-trf-point-system-transport-descent.

proof.text: Form the two natural transformations U_D V_D to F_D S_D given by conjugated I and whiskered J. Localization natural-transformation extensionality reduces their equality to Q(M). Cancel a_D(M) on the source and the two target factorization isomorphisms on the target. Naturality of J and the prescribed descent equation replace J at F_D(Q M) by Q(sigma_(F_c M)). The composition and natural-isomorphism factorization formulas express the derived square isomorphisms in terms of a_c and b_c. The representative equation for I and naturality of the V-factorization then reduce the remaining equality to Q of the assumed chain-level square. Functoriality of Q gives the equality. Evaluate it at X. Identity functors and zero transformations are covered by the same cancellations; no boundedness is needed.

    (τ : U.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ) ⟶ U'.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ))
    (σ : R.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ) ⟶ S.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ))
    (I : U.mapDerivedCategory ⟶ U'.mapDerivedCategory)
    (J : R.mapDerivedCategory ⟶ S.mapDerivedCategory)
    (hI : ∀ X, I.app (DerivedCategory.Q.obj X) ≫
      U'.mapDerivedCategoryFactors.hom.app X =
        U.mapDerivedCategoryFactors.hom.app X ≫ DerivedCategory.Q.map (τ.app X))
    (hJ : ∀ X, J.app (DerivedCategory.Q.obj X) ≫
      S.mapDerivedCategoryFactors.hom.app X =
        R.mapDerivedCategoryFactors.hom.app X ≫ DerivedCategory.Q.map (σ.app X))
    (h : ∀ X, (V.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).map (τ.app X) ≫
      (NatTrans.mapHomologicalComplex b.hom (.up ℤ)).app X =
        (NatTrans.mapHomologicalComplex a.hom (.up ℤ)).app X ≫
          σ.app ((F.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj X))
    (X : DerivedCategory A) :
    ((Functor.mapDerivedCategoryCompIso U V).symm ≪≫
        Functor.mapDerivedCategoryNatIso a ≪≫
        Functor.mapDerivedCategoryCompIso F R).inv.app X ≫
      V.mapDerivedCategory.map (I.app X) ≫
      ((Functor.mapDerivedCategoryCompIso U' V).symm ≪≫
        Functor.mapDerivedCategoryNatIso b ≪≫
        Functor.mapDerivedCategoryCompIso F S).hom.app X =
      J.app (F.mapDerivedCategory.obj X)
